name: Coffee still awake at midnight

subject: a huge white coffee mug on the bedside table, about 40% of the frame height, with the caffeine bean in it
face: the caffeine bean in the mug: bulging wired eyes with take lines and a tight manic grin, eyes locked on the sleeping bea
why: Anyone with an afternoon coffee wonders if it's still working while they sleep, and the video answers exactly that with the 3 p.m. maths (roughly 30 mg still in you at midnight, nine hours later) and the review's suggestion to stop about nine hours before bed.
risk: It could suggest everyone still carries a strong dose at midnight, or that the bean drank coffee at bedtime; the mug is drawn empty and steamless, and the video gives the 2-to-8-hour half-life range and calls its numbers an example.

name: Mug burglar with a sack
concept: A flat ink-black bedroom at night with a yellow moon in the window; the YOU bean sleeps contentedly in bed left of centre while a giant white coffee mug wearing a black robber's eye mask tiptoes away on little legs towards the centre-right, a bulging yellow sack printed with a crescent moon and star
subject: the masked coffee mug carrying a sack of sleep
face: the mug's face: a smug, sly grin, eyes sliding back over its shoulder at the sleeper
why: A coffee cup sneaking off with your night is funny and readable at a glance, the number puts a price on it, and the video pays it off with the 2023 review of 24 studies (about 45 minutes less sleep on average) and its own line about 'the most polite kind of theft'.
risk: The picture mostly restates the title's 'steal', and '-45 MIN' could read as the cost of every single cup; the video frames it as an average across studies with different doses, so it is honest, but it adds the least new information of the top three.

name: Afternoon mug, midnight mug
concept: The frame splits down a wavy line: the left 45% is flat yellow afternoon with a sunburst, the right 55% flat ink-black night with a moon, and each half holds the same big see-through glass mug, the left one crammed to the brim with eight tiny wide-eyed red caffeine beans and the right one with two o
subject: two identical glass mugs: full of caffeine beans at 3 PM, still about a quarter full at midnight
face: the YOU bean: shocked disbelief, eyes on the beans left in the midnight mug
why: The visual sum 'still that much, that late?' is instantly readable, and the video does exactly this calculation: a 100 mg cup with a 5-hour half-life leaves about 30 mg, more than a quarter, at midnight.
risk: Two scenes plus a bean is busier at 246 px than one subject and close to the current text, and the quarter depends on a 5-hour half-life; the video states that assumption and the 2-to-8-hour range, and filling the mugs with beans rather than coffee avoids implying an unfinished drink.

name: Coffee with a dead battery

subject: a giant steaming coffee mug with an empty battery on its front
face: the YOU bean: shocked disbelief, eyes on the battery
why: 'Coffee gives you no energy' contradicts what nearly everyone believes, and the video pays it off early: black coffee has about two calories, and caffeine works by blocking the tiredness signal, not by adding fuel.
